perspective:
John Atcitty’s available information:

- He is an Alaska Native heavy equipment operator with a middle-school education. He teaches equipment operation at the community center.
- Beverly Yan is his colleague there, an adult education teacher with a doctorate. He respects her skills and feels insecure about his education compared with hers.
- In their joint class project, John set up the equipment and told Beverly he hoped it met her expectations. He heard Beverly say she admired how he handled machines and that education is about what you do with what you know.
- After Beverly praised his machinery expertise, John thanked her and proposed a new workshop combining theory and practice. He heard Beverly love the idea, call his practical skills invaluable, and say they could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, John worried Beverly might have higher expectations and felt pressured. He told her he might not always meet the high standards. He heard Beverly appreciate his honesty, suggest realistic goals, and say their combined efforts—not perfection—made projects successful.
- After their frank discussion, John felt Beverly valued his honesty and saw him as a reliable partner. He told her he was glad they talked and that being open with her mattered to him. He heard Beverly respect his openness, trust his judgment completely, and ask to keep transparency going.
- Encouraged by their successful collaborations and perceived mutual respect, John proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase their achievements. He heard Beverly call it fantastic, say it was the perfect way to demonstrate their impact, and agree to start planning.
- He knows they have collaborated successfully and are planning further joint work/events.
